root_cause_analysis: The eval runner supplies C22 ground-truth business_date 2026-06-03 and business_today 2026-06-04 through per-case Settings. The memory-prelude run proves that this date context is executable: detect_anomaly persisted E1, used current date 2026-06-03, baseline dates 2026-05-27/2026-05-20/2026-05-13/2026-05-06, and correctly returned no_anomaly. The main run failed earlier: agent_run has target_date=2026-06-03 but metric_id is null, status=failed, error_code=DATE_RANGE_INVALID, with zero trace_step rows and zero sql_audit rows. That places the failure inside MetricService.parse_question / LLMIntentPlanner before plan compilation. The likely mechanism is that the LLM intent boundary did not reliably honor RUN TARGET DATE for the relative-date phrase "two days ago" and emitted DATE_RANGE_INVALID or a current/future target date that MetricService rejected.

proposed_fix.description: Strengthen the intent/date-context contract so relative-date or generic anomaly questions with a configured run_target_date cannot fail as DATE_RANGE_INVALID when the run_target_date is before business_today. Keep fail-fast semantics for true multi-day ranges and future dates; do not change eval runner, scorer, ground truth, discovery, ranking, or baseline SQL. Add a C22 regression proving parse_question with Settings(target_date=2026-06-03) and business_today=2026-06-04 returns ParsedIntent(metric_id=gmv, target_date=2026-06-03, question_family=gmv_drop) for "Was GMV abnormal two days ago?".
proposed_fix.estimated_impact: C22 main phase should parse the same per-case date context already proven by the memory phase, reach detect_anomaly, and return no_anomaly. The fix should not affect multi-signal discovery lanes, ranking, merge weights, SQL rendering, or evidence aliases.
proposed_fix.negative_fix_warning: Do not mask DATE_RANGE_INVALID globally, do not default every invalid date to settings.target_date, and do not hardcode C22 or the phrase "two days ago". The contract must remain typed and fail-fast for unsupported multi-day ranges and true current/future dates.
